data.title: RATP Dev to grow share of e-buses in Nancy public transport fleet
data.description: From January 2027, RATP Dev will operate public transport in and around the French city of Nancy for seven years. The operator aims to increase the share of battery buses and trolleybuses in the 257-vehicle fleet from 11 to 35 per cent by 2033.

data.title: Cylib opens door for investment by German Federal Agency for Disruptive Innovation
data.description: SPRIND, the German Federal Agency for Disruptive Innovation, is participating in Aachen-based battery recycling specialist Cylib. The startup, founded in 2022, is close to commercialising its processes. Cylib's hydrometallurgical recycling plant is currently being built in Dormagen, North Rhine-Westphalia.

data.title: VinFast unveils new VF 5 and VF 6 with refreshed design, improved range
data.description: Vietnamese automaker VinFast has unveiled facelifted versions of the VF 5 and VF 6 small electric SUVs, both with revised styling, longer driving ranges, and new quality-of-life features. The company has launched both updated EVs first in its home market and expects to commence deliveries after Lunar New Year, which falls on 6 February 2027.

data.title: Volgren delivers 95 electric buses to Transport for NSW
data.description: Australian bus manufacturer Volgren has completed delivery of 95 battery-electric buses to Transport for NSW. The fleet was delivered in just seven months and will be operated by Transit Systems Australia from the Leichhardt depot in Sydney.

data.title: GM adds ‘plug & charge’ to Electrify America charging hubs
data.description: EV drivers enrolled in GM's Energy Pass service now have access to 'plug & charge' capabilities at participating Electrify America fast-charging hubs in the US. This allows compatible vehicles to start charging simply by connecting the cable - without the need for an app, touchscreen or payment card.

data.title: New Jersey awards nearly $15 million for electric schoolbuses
data.description: The New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) has awarded nearly $15 million in grants to school districts and transport providers to purchase 44 battery-electric schoolbuses and install 40 associated charging stations.

data.title: EU statistics reveal sales trends for battery-electric trucks and tractor units
data.description: The sales of electric commercial vehicles vary depending on the vehicle structure: conventional trucks already account for a higher share of electric vehicles than tractors. This is revealed by an analysis of the Federal Statistical Office, drawing on data from the European statistical authority Eurostat.

data.title: BAIC sells 112 battery swap stations, shifts focus to CATL
data.description: BAIC plans to sell assets related to 112 of its own battery swap stations as it more closely aligns its swap strategy with CATL's Choco-Swap network. The minimum price for the package is approximately 278 million yuan.

data.title: India: Delhivery to add up to 2,000 electric light commercial vehicles
data.description: Indian logistics service provider Delhivery has announced plans to deploy between 1,500 and 2,000 electric small trucks over the next 12 to 18 months. The company will use the new EVs for its intra-city logistics operations.

data.title: Mercedes-Benz VLE production finalises in China
data.description: Three months after applying for local sales approval, the first series-production vehicles of the new electric VLE van are now rolling off the production line at Mercedes-Benz's Chinese plant. With this, the Stuttgart-based automaker is setting the stage for the market launch in the People's Republic just before the public premiere at the Guangzhou Auto Show.

data.title: E.ON and BMW expand V2G offering for Neue Klasse models
data.description: In addition to the pioneering BMW iX3, further models from the Neue Klasse series can now use V2G functions. The technical prerequisite is the sixth generation BMW eDrive technology, which debuted with the iX3.

data.title: BMZ integrates digital battery passports into series production
data.description: BMZ, together with Minespider, is introducing digital battery passports for its EU production in Germany and Poland. The passports are to be created directly using production data and will meet the requirements of the EU Battery Regulation starting February 2027.

data.title: VW secures trademark rights for ‘ID. UP’
data.description: A new entry from VW has appeared at the EUIPO, the EU Intellectual Property Office. The company has applied to register the name ID. UP. This suggests that the upcoming electric model will also bear this name. A report from Portugal already mentions the production of the first pre-series vehicles.

data.title: EU accelerates approvals for power grids and charging stations
data.description: The European Parliament and EU member states have reached a provisional agreement to streamline approval procedures for grid connections, charging stations, storage systems, and more. As part of this, the construction of charging stations with up to one megawatt in "artificial structures" is expected to become exempt from approval in the future.

data.title: CATL to become market leader in passenger car battery swapping
data.description: CATL could become the largest battery swap station operator for passenger cars in China next year. The company plans to have 6,000 stations in operation by 2027. According to Chinese industry portals, this should be enough to overtake Nio’s slower-growing battery swapping network.

data.title: US researchers identify electrode drying risk during fast charging
data.description: Researchers at the University of Maryland have found that lithium ions carry solvent molecules with them as they move through a battery. During fast charging, however, the solvent may not flow back quickly enough, causing the positive electrode to dry out and slowing the charging process.

data.title: Envoy and LACI launch EV car-sharing initiative in New Jersey
data.description: The partners will deploy up to 30 shared EVs in Hudson and Bergen counties. An $8.5 million (around €7.8 million) state grant funds the project to expand electric mobility in underserved communities.

data.title: Rolls-Royce Phantom VI swaps V8 for electric powertrain
data.description: Electrogenic has converted a 1973 Rolls-Royce Phantom VI to electric drive. The official representative limousine of the City of London now has 120 kW of power, a 62 kWh battery and charging capacity of up to 100 kW.

data.title: Denza enters India, simultaneously launches D9 and Z9 GT
data.description: After launching operations in Europe earlier this year, BYD Group's premium and luxury brand Denza has entered the Indian market. The company has launched the D9 MPV and Z9 GT shooting brake as its first two models in the country.

data.title: M&H Carriers deploys 18 new eSprinters for deliveries across northern Scotland
data.description: The Scottish haulier and distributor M&H Carriers has expanded its fleet by 18 new Mercedes-Benz eSprinters. They will be operating across the Highlands and north-east Scotland. With increased range, the new electric vans will be able to manage long routes to remote communities even during cold weather periods.
